prompt: For $p(x) = (x - 3)^2(x + 1)$, at which $x$-value does the graph BOUNCE off the $x$-axis instead of crossing it?
hint: Look at the exponents on the factors. One of them is squared.

hints.text: Look at the exponents on the factors. One of them is squared.
An EVEN exponent means the graph touches and bounces. An odd exponent means it crosses.
$(x - 3)^2$ has exponent 2, so the graph bounces at $x = 3$.

explanation: Multiplicity is how many times a factor appears.
$(x - 3)$ appears twice — even multiplicity — so the graph bounces at $x = 3$.
$(x + 1)$ appears once — odd — so the graph crosses at $x = -1$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Watch the sign around the point
steps: Just left of 3, $(x - 3)$ is negative; squaring it makes it positive.
Just right of 3, it is positive; squaring keeps it positive.
The sign never flips, so the graph cannot pass through — it kisses the axis and bounces.
